newsitem.title: USA: GM to build trucks, sport utility at Texas plant.
newsitem.headline: GM to build trucks, sport utility at Texas plant.

text.p: General Motors Corp.'s Arlington, Tex., plant will produce Chevrolet and GMC C/K pickup trucks and Tahoe and Yukon sport/utility vehicles, starting late next year, the automaker said Friday.
The plant now builds GM's Chevrolet Caprice, Buick Roadmaster and Cadillac Fleetwood cars, which will be phased out by the end of this year.

The company had said it would convert the plant from car to truck manufacturing but had not identified specific products. The automaker is investing about $260 million in the Arlington conversion project.

GM said the pickup trucks built at Arlington will be extended-cab models with an optional third door, providing a second source for the popular vehicles. The company now builds the trucks in Oshawa, Ontario.
The plant also will become the sole source for a new police version of the Chevrolet Tahoe.
GM said the conversion of the plant to truck production will be completed in the second quarter of 1997.

The project is part of a long-term plan GM has to boost truck production to more than 50 percent of its total North American capacity. For the first six months of 1996, trucks made up about 45 percent of GM's output.
